title: Melania Trump and LSU are set to announce a scholarship program for students who were in foster care
text:
WASHINGTON (AP) — Melania Trump was headed to Louisiana on Saturday to announce a partnership between Louisiana State University and her “Fostering the Future” program to provide scholarships for LSU students who came through the foster care system.
The first lady also planned to attend the LSU-Alabama football game in the afternoon.
The foster care program will be featured across the LSU campus in Baton Rouge as well as on the field at Tiger Stadium just before kickoff, the White House said.
Trump and LSU secured $5 million to create an endowment fund for the scholarships, the White House said. It provided no details on the source of the money.
The first lady started working on foster care issues after President Donald Trump’s first term ended in 2021, and created “Fostering the Future” to provide resources and support, including scholarships. LSU is among more than 20 colleges and universities nationwide that participate in the program.
Earlier this year, Melania Trump was on Capitol Hill to push Congress to pass a legislative package that would broaden access to services for young people in foster care by updating a decades-old program. The measures cleared the House and are pending in the Senate.
During the appearance, she told members of the House Ways and Means Committee that young people in foster care face barriers to housing, transportation and other challenges outside of the classroom that affect their performance in school along with their future financial independence.
“We can close this gap,” she said in April. “New legislation for the foster care community is a moral imperative.”
Last November, the first lady spearheaded an executive order signed by the Republican president linking the federal government, colleges and universities, the private sector and charitable groups to create educational and employment opportunities for those in foster care.
She also created “Fostering the Future Together,” a global version of the program with more than 45 participating countries.
Alabama and LSU, meanwhile, are historical regional rivals and both teams entered the week in contention for a College Football Playoff berth.
Donald Trump has attended two prior LSU games as president: one at Alabama in 2019 and one in New Orleans in January 2020, when LSU defeated Clemson for the national championship. Melania Trump accompanied him to the second game.
The president was not scheduled to attend Saturday’s game.

AP Sports Writer Brett Martel in Baton Rouge, La., contributed to this report.

title: Foxcroft Academy field hockey wins 2nd straight Class C title
text:
Our Communities. Our Teams. Our Future.
We’re proud to make high school sports coverage free for everyone, because these moments matter. At Maine State Credit Union, we’re here for the people and places that make Maine strong. Let’s go! Learn more at mainestatecu.org. 
AUBURN — The Foxcroft Academy field hockey team was leading everywhere. The Ponies were controlling play. They were ahead in corners. They were ahead in shots.
They were ahead everywhere — but the scoreboard. However, as it went into halftime of a scoreless tie, the second-highest scoring team in Maine history figured the goals were coming.
“We knew we were dominating,” sophomore Addie Rayfield said. “(The talk) was, keep shooting, quick shots. They’ll go in at some point.”
Rayfield scored a pair of goals, both assisted by senior Jenna Hartford, and Foxcroft Academy capped another undefeated season with a 2-0 win over Winthrop/Maranacook in the Class C championship game Saturday night at Edward Little High School.
“To be able to do it last year, but also do it again, undefeated as well, is just an even better feeling,” Rayfield said.
The feeling was better, but so were the Ponies (18-0). Foxcroft outscored teams 144-8 this year, and with two goals Saturday passed the 2017 St. Dominic Academy team (143) for second most in state history. Only the 2012 Skowhegan team (155) scored more.
“It’s very special,” Hartford said. “We aimed to try to beat the state record. We got very close.”
Foxcroft had seven corners in the first half and came within feet of getting goals from Kaydiense Nelson and Rayfield, but the Ponies hadn’t broken through on the scoreboard against the Ramblers (16-2). In the second half, that changed.
On the Ponies’ 10th corner, Hartford had a shot that goalie Cyara Harriman saved, but the rebound went to Rayfield and she buried the follow-up with 2:18 to go in the third.
The two players teamed up for the next goal as well. Hartford found Rayfield with a pass through the circle, and the sophomore skipped in a reverse for a 2-0 lead with 9:07 to play.
“We definitely were very nervous, but it wasn’t like a, ‘Oh, are we going to lose?’ (feeling),” Hartford said. “We were just like, ‘We need to up the intensity. We need to keep trying.'”
The two-goal lead was a commanding advantage, as Foxcroft shut down nearly every Winthrop effort to get into its offense. Lilah French and Payson Hall attacked the ball in the infield, and the Ramblers were unable to register a shot on goal.
Rayfield said the Ponies made it a priority to shut down Winthrop’s outlet passes.
“We knew that we had to give it all we got, especially because it’s the last one,” Rayfield said.
Winthrop spent most of the game on defense, but thanks to their backs and Harriman in net, the Ramblers kept it close.
“I can’t say enough about how well we played defensively tonight. We were challenged, just like we knew we would,” Winthrop coach Holly Daigle said. “I am proud of my girls for the effort they gave for the full 60 minutes.”
In her first year after coaching at Cony, Daigle brought the Ramblers back to the state final after they missed it last year following four straight titles.
“We had an extraordinary season,” she said. “I just really wanted it for them. I really did. They deserve to be here.”

title: Much needed soaking rain this weekend and more seasonable temps
text:
BANGOR, Maine (WABI) - The rain that arrived yesterday evening will continue on and off throughout much of the weekend as a weak low pressure system meanders off our coast. While sun won’t be the dominant story as it has been for much of the last two weeks we are in serious need of the rain so I think most of us will trade a sunny weekend for a rainy one considering the drought conditions. While it won’t be an overwhelming amount of rain it certainly will do some damage to the drought. Once it clears later Sunday, the weeks ahead looks calm with much more seasonable (cooler) temps.
Today: Rain most of the day
It will be a chillier and wet Saturday for most. Rain this morning will stick around most of the day but mainly be light. Some heavier showers are possible but for the most part it will be a rainy and wet day with higher amounts of rain falling along the coast. Anywhere from about a quarter of an inch up far to the north to over an inch along coastal locations. It will also be somewhat breezy with some gusts up to 30 mph. Cooler temps arrive as well with highs only in the 40s and 50s.
Tonight: Rain continues for most with some breaks
The rain will continue for a good percentage of everyone overnight as showery activity associated with the slow moving low pressure system continues to inch northeastward. It will likely be heavier along the coast with the possibility to pick up to an inch or so along the coast with a few places inland cashing in to an extent as well depending on where heavier rain may set up. Lows will likely only drop a few degrees in the lower 40s. Breeziness will continue with gusts up to 20-25 mph.
Sunday: Some rain early, then clearing and cooler in the afternoon
The rain will continue in the morning with the chance for some wintry mix across colder spots in the west and the far north on Sunday but will begin to move east as the day goes on. The showers should be out of the state by 4 or 5 pm except for maybe extreme eastern Washington county. Temps will be cool once again with highs only reaching the mid to upper 40s for most.
Sunday night: Rain finally fully departs
After a soggy few days things settle down and a seasonably cool night arrives with some lingering cloudiness. Temps will be in the upper 30s for most.
Monday and beyond: A dry day and a more settled week
Things dry out and Monday looks to be a somewhat cloudy day but otherwise typical November weather with highs in the upper 40s and low 50s. After last week was more active this week looks quieter with few chances of active weather besides the weekend.
We are watching a system for late in the week towards next weekend that could provide some early season snow especially for inland and northern regions. It’s a long way off and there are lots of details to work out but it is something we are watching.
Today: Rainy and cooler. Highs in the 50s. Winds NE at 10-20 mph.
Tonight: Scattered showers otherwise overcast. Lows in the 40s. Winds NE 10-15 mph.
Sunday: Showers early, clearing late. Highs in the upper 40s and low 50s. Winds NE at 10-15 mph.
Sunday night: Rain ends clouds stick around. Lows in the upper 30s and low 40s. Winds NE 5-10 mph then going calm.
Monday: Mostly cloudy but dry. Highs in the upper 40s and low 50s. Winds W 5-10 mph.
Monday night: Still mainly cloudy. Lows in the 30s. Light wind.

In 2013, John Boyko got an idea for a sculpture project in a field at his 40-acre property in Madrid. “I just felt like building a cross,” he said.
Now 88, Boyko is still working on the large-scale depiction of the Crucifixion of Jesus. The cross, which is 800 feet long and 335 feet wide, is comprised of pine and fir trees that are cut short in height, and the face of Jesus is made of stones stacked like a wall and of smaller colored stones depicting his hair and beard. The crown of thorns is made from quarter-inch-thick stainless steel abstract shapes cut by Boyko himself.
In recent years, Boyko has focused on constructing memorial stands that are made from stainless steel, plastic and fiber optic cable that light up at night, and he has converted an old chicken coop into a visitor center where people who stop by can learn more about his project.
“I have a lot more work to do,” Boyko said. “Maybe two more summers’ worth.”

title: In a setback for Netanyahu, Israel’s president taps opposition candidate to form a government
text:
JERUSALEM (AP) — Israeli President Isaac Herzog said Saturday night that he was giving opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot the first opportunity to form a governing coalition following elections on Oct. 27.
Eisenkot, a former military chief who ran as the main challenger to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, is now a step closer to ousting Israel’s longest-serving premier.
“This is the time to establish a national emergency government. I will do anything possible to prove us worthy,” Eisenkot posted on his X account just after the presidential announcement.
He has up to six weeks to form a coalition, a challenging task in a deeply divided country reeling from the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas-led attacks and the three years of wars that have followed in Gaza and beyond.
In discussions with the president this week, representatives from most of Israel’s main parties recommended Eisenkot be tasked with assembling a new government. But putting together the parliamentary majority needed remains fraught and any possible coalition would require candidates to make tough compromises that could outrage their own voters.
Netanyahu and his allies lost their majority in parliament in last month’s elections. But the bloc led by Eisenkot also didn’t win a majority. That left Arab-led parties, which made historic gains, as potential but politically fraught kingmakers.
An Arab party has been part of a governing coalition just once in Israel’s history. Forming such an alliance could be especially divisive for Eisenkot after more than three years of war in Gaza.
Netanyahu has been on a campaign to head off any alliance between Eisenkot and the Arab-led parties, including unsubstantiated claims that Arab parties “stole” the elections. Shortly before Herzog’s announcement, he called for a “national unity government” in a video statement and warned against “hastily swearing in a government with terrorist supporters” – language he uses to refer to the Arab-led parties.
Netanyahu and his allies have repeatedly portrayed the Arab-led parties as a threat to national security, while Eisenkot has indicated a willingness to partner with them under certain conditions, including calling Hamas a terrorist group that needs to be destroyed.
Eisenkot and Netanyahu, whose Likud is the single largest party in parliament, could seek to create a broad unity government with major Jewish parties. However, the men have deep differences over many issues that will be difficult to bridge. That includes Netanyahu’s reliance on religious parties that demand draft exemptions for ultra-Orthodox men, as well as Netanyahu’s opposition to a formal investigation into the security failures surrounding the Oct. 7 attacks.
Eisenkot could also seek to create a “minority” government — shored up by external support from Arab parties that are not formal members of his coalition. However, other members of his bloc have said they would reject such an alliance.
Eisenkot’s party, Yashar, slammed the prime minister’s video with a statement posted on X and urged members of his party, Likud, to disavow their alliance with “radical parties,” in an apparent reference to the far-right parties in his religious-nationalist base.
The statement argued that Eisenkot would only include parties and parliament members who support his party’s principles.
___
Associated Press writers Josef Federman and Julia Frankel contributed from Jerusalem.

title: Time for Senate Democrats to exit hibernation
text:
The country has spoken. I could not be happier with the tsunami of Democrats elected and the new majority in the U.S. House and Senate.
Lots of work needs to be done to repair lots of damage. For that, the Democratic party needs an astute, charismatic leader. A person with new ideas, enthusiasm and the will to make life for us Americans easier. What I have seen in the last nine years under Sen. Schumer’s leadership amounts to pure hibernation.
Some talk about DEI. Yes, equality is important. Just as important, we like to eat, see a medical professional when we are ill, have a job with a livable wage, have a roof over our head and spend time with our kids and family — rather than work two to three jobs to make ends meet.
Congress has a lot of work ahead of it but, please, let’s start with a new and charismatic younger leader of Democrats in the Senate, a person who can relate to the working crowd, to the young families who are struggling to make ends meet as they try to raise healthy, successful children.

title: Let’s talk about how Mainers can reconnect post-election
text:
As if Mother Nature knew we in Maine would need something to rally around this past week, she delivered up meaty material on the best and most cliché small-talk topic of all — the weather — in the form of several unseasonably pleasant fall days.
If the temperature has dropped by the time you read this, remember that there’s plenty else to banter about across party lines: the ever-encroaching onset of Christmas commercials, Tom Brady’s return to Gillette Stadium, the true meaning of the new three-hour documentary “You Can See Everything.”
Residents of Portland, where two in 13 people voted for Sen. Susan Collins, don’t risk offending many neighbors by gloating about the blue wave in public (at least wherever you can buy a matcha latte). In the rest of Maine, however, there’s close to a 50% chance that anyone you encounter at the grocery store or gas station doesn’t share your political views, as big a spread as 6 points might seem on Steve Kornacki’s screen.
So, how, after such a long and contentious election cycle, do we start to find common ground again?
There’s evidence all around that this common ground exists. There even was during the election cycle, when we collectively scoffed at being vote-shamed by Ice-T and brought our concerns about the cost of everything to the polls, albeit with different ideas about who could better address them.
Another unifying factor, unfortunately, is our tendency toward nastiness under pressure, further fueled by the tenor of attack ads. Rather than letting super PACs fan contempt for our neighbors, though, we could try racheting down the rhetoric ourselves.
Longtime News Center Maine anchor Sharon Rose on Wednesday posted a reel to this effect, scolding Democrats for sharing crass memes in the wake of their victory and calling for more respectful discourse. I agree, as she points out, that the hypocrisy of both parties doesn’t help their causes, and that liberals, now out of fight-or-flight mode, are in the better position to change the tone.
Not to say there isn’t a place for sharp criticism, satire or heated debates, but we can have all that and still recognize that being divided on certain topics doesn’t make us wholly different as humans, despite what our political system encourages us to think.
I’ve caught myself, after chuckling at those MAGA rally “gotcha” moments, wondering if the liberal interview style is any less despicable than what Charlie Kirk was doing before he was killed.
The justification for vindictiveness, by both sides, seems to be that our respective underlying values are superior, which is yet another commonality. We all agree on the importance of virtue; we just define it differently.
If that’s what this is about, then, higher morals prevailing, why has it gotten so indecent?
In an interview with “60 Minutes” last weekend, French NBA star Victor Wembanyama was asked about his impression of life in America. Although he likes that people here aren’t judged for being ambitious, he said, he finds social interactions more superficial than in other countries.
Deep conversations certainly haven’t solved France’s problems, but I do think we’d be better served by taking a more genuine interest in each other’s mindset and motivations, the experiences that informed them and our hopes for the future.
That’s not going to happen by talking about the weather, but as a means of initiating a conversation with someone who filled out different bubbles on their ballot than you did on yours, it could be a start.

title: In a setback for Netanyahu, Israel’s president taps opposition candidate to form a government
text:
JERUSALEM (AP) — Israeli President Isaac Herzog said Saturday night that he was giving opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot the first opportunity to form a governing coalition following elections on Oct. 27.
Eisenkot, a former military chief who ran as the main challenger to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, is now a step closer to ousting Israel’s longest-serving premier.
“This is the time to establish a national emergency government. I will do anything possible to prove us worthy,” Eisenkot posted on his X account just after the presidential announcement.
He has up to six weeks to form a coalition, a challenging task in a deeply divided country reeling from the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas-led attacks and the three years of wars that have followed in Gaza and beyond.
In discussions with the president this week, representatives from most of Israel’s main parties recommended Eisenkot be tasked with assembling a new government. But putting together the parliamentary majority needed remains fraught and any possible coalition would require candidates to make tough compromises that could outrage their own voters.
Netanyahu and his allies lost their majority in parliament in last month’s elections. But the bloc led by Eisenkot also didn’t win a majority. That left Arab-led parties, which made historic gains, as potential but politically fraught kingmakers.
An Arab party has been part of a governing coalition just once in Israel’s history. Forming such an alliance could be especially divisive for Eisenkot after more than three years of war in Gaza.
Netanyahu has been on a campaign to head off any alliance between Eisenkot and the Arab-led parties, including unsubstantiated claims that Arab parties “stole” the elections. Shortly before Herzog’s announcement, he called for a “national unity government” in a video statement and warned against “hastily swearing in a government with terrorist supporters” – language he uses to refer to the Arab-led parties.
Netanyahu and his allies have repeatedly portrayed the Arab-led parties as a threat to national security, while Eisenkot has indicated a willingness to partner with them under certain conditions, including calling Hamas a terrorist group that needs to be destroyed.
Eisenkot and Netanyahu, whose Likud is the single largest party in parliament, could seek to create a broad unity government with major Jewish parties. However, the men have deep differences over many issues that will be difficult to bridge. That includes Netanyahu’s reliance on religious parties that demand draft exemptions for ultra-Orthodox men, as well as Netanyahu’s opposition to a formal investigation into the security failures surrounding the Oct. 7 attacks.
Eisenkot could also seek to create a “minority” government — shored up by external support from Arab parties that are not formal members of his coalition. However, other members of his bloc have said they would reject such an alliance.
Eisenkot’s party, Yashar, slammed the prime minister’s video with a statement posted on X and urged members of his party, Likud, to disavow their alliance with “radical parties,” in an apparent reference to the far-right parties in his religious-nationalist base.
The statement argued that Eisenkot would only include parties and parliament members who support his party’s principles.
___
Associated Press writers Josef Federman and Julia Frankel contributed from Jerusalem.

title: Man on probation for child pornography sentenced to life in prison
text:
AMARILLO, Texas (KFDA/Gray News) - A Texas man who was on probation for possessing child pornography will now spend the rest of his life in prison.
Michael Lee Green, 43, appeared before Judge Dee Johnson of Randall County’s 47th District Court on Friday.
Texas authorities said an investigation started in November 2024 when Amarillo Police Department’s Special Victims Unit received a tip from Oklahoma Predator Prevention, an advocacy group that targets online predators.
The tip involved the online activities of Green.
Police investigated the tip, and a department investigator had a forensic examination conducted on Green’s cellphone.
The examination revealed that Green possessed illegal child sexual abuse material involving minors.
Authorities said Green admitted during several interviews with investigators that he received and viewed the material.
He was booked into Randall County Jail on 10 counts of possessing child pornography involving more than 50 depictions or videos of minors.
In March 2025, Green was placed on deferred adjudication for a term of 10 years.
Court records showed that Green was then booked into Randall County Jail again in July on a felony charge of unauthorized absence from a community correction facility.
The offense was related to an incident where he did not report to a court-ordered supervision facility.
At his Friday hearing, Judge Johnson heard evidence from both sides on revocation and punishment.
After hearing the evidence, the judge revoked Green’s probation and sentenced him to life in prison on each of the 10 counts.
Green additionally entered a plea in his other open felony case.

Gorham farm market to reimburse customers who bought invasive maple trees
Customers who purchased certain maple trees from King's Farm Market between May and September 2026 may be eligible for reimbursement
Gorham farm market to reimburse customers who bought invasive maple trees
Customers who purchased certain maple trees from King's Farm Market between May and September 2026 may be eligible for reimbursement
A Gorham farm market has agreed to reimburse customers who purchased invasive maple trees earlier this year, according to the Maine Department of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry.
In a social media post, the department said King's Farm Market will reimburse customers who purchased Crimson King Norway maple trees or Flame Amur maple trees between May and September 2026.
Customers are being asked to contact King's Farm Market at 207-839-5844 if they wish to obtain reimbursement.
According to the department, Norway maple and Amur maple trees compete with native plants and spread into natural areas.
Both species and their varieties and hybrids have been prohibited for sale or import in Maine since 2018.
The department says removing the purchased trees can help prevent future spread.
Customers who need guidance on removing the trees can contact the Maine Department of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry.
More information about prohibited invasive plants is available on the state's website.

title: Letter: Susan Collins’ career ended like Tom Brady’s

I think Susan Collins fell victim to the Tom Brady syndrome. Brady was destined to go out at the top of his game, a multiple Super Bowl winner, affectionately known as the Greatest of All Time. He talked about quitting, but apparently his ego would not let him do it, so he stuck around for another season and then left as a loser.

title: A Hermon High grad could be the new face of Trump's White House
text:
This story has been updated to include White’s response.
A Hermon High School grad could be the White House’s new public face as President Donald Trump moves into his lame duck era.
In a social media post on Saturday, Trump announced that he had asked Dana White, the CEO of the Ultimate Fighting Championship who graduated from Hermon in 1987, to be his press secretary.
“I am pleased to announce that the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior, has been offered the job of Press Secretary of the United States,” Trump posted on his social media platform Truth Social. “Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other. Dana, please take the job!”
White, a longtime friend and Trump ally, is considering the offer, according to the Associated Press. He told reporters at a news conference after a boxing event in London that he planned to fly to Washington to discuss the idea with the president on Monday.
If he accepts, the move would elevate someone with deep ties to the Bangor area to one of the most public-facing roles in federal government. White owns property in Bangor and Levant, where he spent time visiting his grandparents and cousins as a kid. In 2011, he donated $100,000 to upgrade Hermon High School’s athletic complex.
“My time up there meant so much to me and I loved the place so much that I bought the whole street that my grandmother and grandfather lived on,” he told the Bangor Daily News in early 2025, shortly after he attended Trump’s second inauguration. “I went house to house, knocked on everyone’s door and asked if they would sell me their house.”
He would be an unorthodox pick for press secretary only by traditional measures. The president has favored allies, media personalities, and those with a pugnacious streak for his cabinet. In June, White hosted a UFC event on the White House lawn.
He would be the third to serve in the role since Trump retook office. Karoline Leavitt, the youngest person to ever become press secretary, stepped down in August. Her successor, political commentator Katie Zacharia, lasted just five days after bumbling through her first appearance with reporters and misrepresenting her credentials as a lawyer.
It was initially unclear on Saturday if White planned to accept the job or how serious Trump’s surprise offer really was. The New York Times had suggested the move, real or a joke, was meant to demonstrate the president’s defiance in the wake of a Republican wipeout in Tuesday’s midterm elections widely viewed as a repudiation of his policies. Democrats recaptured both chambers of Congress by sizable margins, including Senate seats in deep-red territory like Texas and Kansas.

title: Hall-Dale boys soccer holds off Fort Kent for 3rd straight Class C title
text:
We’re proud to make high school sports coverage free for everyone, because these moments matter. At Maine State Credit Union, we’re here for the people and places that make Maine strong. Let’s go! Learn more at mainestatecu.org. 
LEWISTON — Greyson Cary was frustrated. The Hall-Dale junior had multiple opportunities in the first half of the Class C boys soccer final, but was unable to put one in the net.
A perfect pass and a open look ended that frustration for Carey, who delivered a goal and a third straight state championship for Bulldogs.
Carey scored with 19:44 left in the second half, the only goal in Hall-Dale’s 1-0 victory over Fort Kent on Saturday at Lewiston High School.
“It feels as good as the first and the second (title), but it feels good that we have a group of kids who get to celebrate again today,” said Hall-Dale coach Jesse Rowe. “You set out for these the day after the last (season) finishes, so tomorrow we’ll be preparing for the future. But they’ll enjoy the next 24 hours, for sure.”
Hall-Dale finishes 17-1-0. Fort Kent, the C North champion, ends 10-7-1.
Senior forward Collin McArthur sent an accurate pass to Cary, who promptly knocked it into the low corner to give Hall-Dale the lead.
“You live those moments in your head so often,” said Cary. “You just have to turn off your brain, just do what you’ve been practicing and just finish the goal.”
McArthur added: “We worked (on the play) all through practice, we knew (Fort Kent) was going to play a sweeper. We planned those diagonal runs and try to see where we could find Greyson, or Karter (Eldridge), or me in that slot. (Cary) yelled my name, I saw him, and he took it from there.”
Cary had two near-goal opportunities in the first half, one shot that went wide, another stopped on a diving save by Fort Kent goalie Kyle Paradis.
“It’s been frustrating, a little bit,” Cary said. “But you just have to be patient, recognize the work, and just let the play come to me.”
The first half of the game was a showcase of goalies. Paradis, a junior, made five saves before halftime, including a diving save to his right on Cary’s shot with 8:45 remaining in the half. The Bulldogs had a 6-2 shot advantage in the first half.
Paradis finished with seven saves.
“He’s an incredible (goalie),” Fort Kent coach Kalusha Kotes said of Paradis. “It wasn’t the result we wanted (today), but I’m confident we will be back.”
While less busy, the work was no less dramatic for Hall-Dale keeper Landon Gilbert. He made a jumping save on a 50-yard indirect kick from Fort Kent’s Dominic Cyr. With 5:40 remaining in the first half, Cyr had Gilbert on a one-on-one breakaway situation, but Cyr’s shot went wide to the left.
Gilbert finished with three saves. All three Hall-Dale title wins have been by 1-0 scores. The Bulldogs beat Washington Academy in 2024 and Orono last year.

title: US military carries out new targeted strikes on Iran as Tehran's leaders weigh mediator's proposals
text:
US military carries out new targeted strikes on Iran as Tehran's leaders weigh mediator's proposals
President Donald Trump said the U.S. military on Friday carried out new limited strikes on Iran, targeting an Iranian air defense system.
Iranian state media reported the sound of two explosions in the Suza area of Qeshm Island, which is in the crucial waterway for oil shipments.
Trump in an exchange with reporters described the military action as "minor."
"They knocked out -- they built a little bit of an anti-aircraft device and we knocked it out in about 15 minutes, maybe five," Trump told reporters shortly after arriving in West Palm Beach, Florida, on Friday evening.
Trump did not offer further details about the target. But U.S. officials have reported that most of Iran's air defense systems were destroyed or severely degraded during a June 2025 bombardment by Israel and in the early stages of the current conflict. U.S. officials have assessed that Iran would try to rebuild them and other military infrastructure over time.
The U.S. military also reported carrying out what it described as defensive strikes on Monday. Explosions were heard on the islands of Qeshm and Hengam in the strategic Strait of Hormuz, and in the nearby mainland area of Bandar Abbas.
Friday's strikes are the first since Trump's Republican Party was dealt a stunning repudiation in Tuesday's midterm elections in the U.S.
The electoral setback — Republicans lost both chambers of Congress — was stoked in part by voter dissatisfaction with Trump's execution of the conflict and elevated fuel prices, a byproduct of the war that's affected nearly every sector of the global economy.
In the days since Republicans' shellacking at the polls, Trump has vacillated between threatening to "destroy" Iran and suggesting a resolution to the war is near.
Qatar presents new proposals to Iranian officials
Earlier Friday, two Middle East government officials said Iran was reviewing proposals presented by chief mediator Qatar aimed at addressing differences with the United States about Tehran's nuclear program.
But one of the officials stressed that the Iranians, at least at the moment, remain unwilling to engage in negotiations with the Trump administration over their atomic activities until the U.S. agrees to several core conditions that Iran has been demanding be part of any ceasefire agreement.
Differences with Iran over its nuclear program remain the thorniest issue and one that Trump insists must be resolved as part of any deal meant to end the more than 8-month-old war.
Both officials were not authorized to comment publicly on the delicate negotiations and spoke on the condition of anonymity.
Meanwhile, U.S. Central Command, which oversees U.S. military operations in the Middle East, announced in a post on X late Friday that the United States was offering "a reward of up to $20 million and possible relocation for information about Iran's nuclear program, including its facilities, equipment, and associated personnel, such as those in the scientific community, or the movement of any of the above."
The post included a link to the State Department's Rewards for Justice program.
Iran insists on several concessions before nuclear talks
The White House declined to comment about the Qatari-presented proposals on Iran's nuclear program, but Trump noted earlier Friday in an exchange with reporters that mediators' discussions with Iran continue.
"We are talking to Iran. We have been," said Trump, who insists the U.S. military remains in control of the conflict with a battered Iran.
Yet, Tehran insists on several concessions from the U.S., which Trump has declined in the past. Among the core demands Iran says must be met before engaging in nuclear talks: ending the U.S. blockade on Iran's ports, lifting sanctions, unfreezing its assets, issuing compensation for war damage and ending hostilities throughout the region, including Israeli operations in Lebanon.
Qataris and Iranians discuss a bridge deal to get to nuclear talks
Mediators and Iran have discussed a potential bridge deal aimed at helping pave the way for further talks on Tehran's nuclear program, according to regional officials.
They said the proposal, which was recently presented to the two sides by Qatari mediators, called for implementing trust-building measures over the course of two days.
These measures include lifting the U.S. blockade and releasing some of the billions of dollars in Iranian frozen funds seized over the years as part of a U.S. campaign to isolate Iran over its nuclear program. In return, Tehran would allow International Atomic Energy Agency inspectors at its sites bombed by the U.S. and Israel, the officials said.
On the second day, Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz in line with a modified agreement that Iran and Oman have reached on the waterway but has not been approved by the United States, the officials said. That mechanism would be temporary until a permanent deal is reached on the strait in cooperation with other Gulf countries, they said.
Following the implementation of the measures, the U.S. and Iran would embark on extensive talks addressing Iran's stockpile of highly enriched uranium as well as other aspects of its program, the officials said.
Iran has long maintained that its nuclear program is peaceful. According to the International Atomic Energy Agency, Iran has 440.9 kilograms (972 pounds) of uranium that is enriched up to 60% purity, a short, technical step from weapons-grade levels of 90%.
Diplomatic efforts pick up following US election
A flurry of diplomatic phone calls in recent days between leaders in the Persian Gulf and beyond has been aimed at easing tensions in the region. Concerns have mounted over the possibility that Trump could still order the U.S. military to carry out new strikes against Iran.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth spoke Friday with his Qatari counterpart, Sheikh Saoud bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, about developments, according to the Qatari government.
The Qatari government announced the call between the countries' defense officials after confirming earlier Friday that Trump and Qatar's emir had a separate call to discuss efforts to deescalate tensions.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi also held phone calls with his Iraqi and Tunisian counterparts on Friday to discuss tensions in the region. Araghchi and Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein discussed Tehran's vision for resuming negotiations with the U.S., according to Iraq's News Agency.
Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty, who held two calls with Araghchi this week, said Friday in a post on X that it was critical that both sides demonstrate "flexibility" to achieve the "compromise solutions" necessary to prevent the region from sliding into a new wave of escalation.
Egypt's top diplomat also held a phone call with his Emirati counterpart, Abdullah Bin Zayed Al Nahyan, to emphasize the importance of political negotiations to prevent another military confrontation that could fuel violence and destruction, according to a statement by Egypt's Foreign Ministry.

title: Penobscot Valley girls soccer edges Monmouth Academy to win Class D title
text:
Our Communities. Our Teams. Our Future.
We’re proud to make high school sports coverage free for everyone, because these moments matter. At Maine State Credit Union, we’re here for the people and places that make Maine strong. Let’s go! Learn more at mainestatecu.org. 
OAKLAND — McKenna Ireland earned playing time as an eighth-grader late last season in Penobscot Valley’s state title run.
A year later in the Class D state championship game, Ireland scored the Gold Ball-clinching goal.
Ireland’s goal Saturday gave Penobscot Valley a 1-0 win over Monmouth Academy in the Class D state championship game at Messalonskee High School.
“(Ireland) came in clutch for us last year as an eighth-grader … and I think that benefited her in a big way this year to come in and not be as nervous,” said coach Lana Cummings. “And she can hold her own out there, for sure.”
The Howlers capped another successful playoff run by beating the Mustangs, who made their first state final appearance in 26 years.
“It’s crazy,” Penobscot Valley keeper Brooklynn Raymond said. “Everybody doubted us. They said we weren’t going to be the same team, that we were rebuilding. And we knew we just had to believe in each other and we had a coaching staff that believed in us and pushed us every day, and it’s amazing just to know we could make it here again.”
Monmouth (10-7) didn’t make it easy on three-time defending champion Penobscot Valley (11-3-4). The Mustangs took nine shots on goal to the Howlers’ one in the first half, and both teams had four apiece in the second half.
Penobscot Valley broke through when Ireland scored on a breakaway four and a half minutes into the second half.
“It was just all so fast,” Ireland said. “I was just so grateful that my team could set me up for that goal. I wasn’t the reason why we won, it was my whole team working together and setting everybody up to win.”
Monmouth nearly scored on several occasions, including a deflection of a cross that went just wide with under 10 seconds to play.
“We were real close,” co-Monmouth coach Haley Fletcher-Springer said. “We had a lot of opportunities and we unfortunately just couldn’t finish those opportunities. And (the Howlers) capitalized on their opportunities, so props to them. Stinks to go out this way, for sure, but really proud of our team.”
Raymond was a force all game, finishing with 13 saves. A senior, she was a state champion every year of her career.
“I looked at Coach after the game, I said, ‘I maxed out my career and it still doesn’t feel like it was enough,’” Raymond said. “So just being a part of something this special has been amazing, and it’s tough. It’s going to be hard not coming back next year.”

title: Footage shows bodies at the home of the man behind mass shooting in Polish city, prime minister says
text:
KRAKOW, Poland (AP) — A Polish man with far-right views drove into a busy central square in Krakow on Saturday and opened fire, killing six people and injuring 15 others before police shot and wounded him, authorities said.
The attack, which Poland’s defense minister described as an “act of terror,” happened in Main Square, which is in the heart of Krakow’s Old Town and is a major tourist hub in the country’s second-largest city.
The 25-year-old attacker drove to multiple spots in the square and opened fire at each stop with an automatic weapon, authorities said. Although they didn’t release his name, Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński said the man holds “very radical” and “ultranationalistic” views.
“Everything indicates that he was fascinated by far-right ideologies,” Kierwiński said at a news conference.
Hours after the attack, Prime Minister Donald Tusk said authorities found the bodies of three of the suspect’s close family members — two women and a man — inside of his home in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski, a city about 150 kilometers (93 miles) northeast of Krakow.
“We have the next acts of this tragedy,” Tusk told reporters.
Four women and two men were killed in the Krakow attack. At least three of the women were Polish, and one of the dead was a U.K. citizen, authorities said. Police were still trying to identify the other two people who were killed.
A total of 13 people were hospitalized in serious condition, authorities said, though that figure may include the gunman, who underwent surgery after the attack.
It’s unclear how many of the injured were shot. Two of them were treated and released within hours of the mass shooting. Two police officers were seriously injured, Kierwiński said. Five non-Poles were also injured, police commander Marek Boroń said.
People were wounded at several locations
The attacker wore military-style fatigues and a bulletproof vest, and used a military-type long gun, Krakow police spokesperson Katarzyna Cisło said. Police found other weapons and ammunition in his car. He kept firing at the police even after being shot himself, she said.
The attacker engaged in a “wild ride” around Main Square, which is why people were wounded at several locations, said Cisło, adding that the gunman appears to have acted alone.
Krakow mayor Łukasz Gibała said the city will be in official mourning until Wednesday. He vowed that Krakow will remain open to visitors despite the tragedy.
“The square will belong to us again,” Gibała said in a video posted on X.
Mass shootings are rare in Poland
Videos posted on social media by witnesses show people running away from the square to take cover on small streets nearby, as well as first responders trying to resuscitate victims. In one video, a police officer is seen repeatedly shooting the attacker, who is lying on the street, only to later slowly collapse himself to the ground.
Photos showed a Polish Medical Air Rescue helicopter after it landed in the square.
It wasn’t immediately clear whether the gun used in the attack or those found in the attacker’s car are legal. Around 411,000 people hold gun permits in Poland, which has a population of 37 million, and interest in gun ownership has been rising.
Mass shootings are uncommon in Poland. However, in mid-October three attacks at schools in the central province of Mazovia took place within four days, leaving one person dead and many wounded, including children.
The Krakow attacker’s military gear, guns and overall look were similar to those of other “extreme right lone actors” committing attacks around Europe, said Kacper Rekawek, a senior researcher at the International Center for Counterterrorism in The Hague. “We have had attempts before, but now we can say that these kinds of attacks have become successful in Poland.”
Warsaw mayor Rafał Trzaskowski announced increased security measures, including road barriers, along main streets in the old town in the Polish capital in the aftermath of the Krakow attack.
———
Ciobanu reported from Warsaw, Poland, and Dazio reported from Berlin.

title: Human remains found inside burning car at neighborhood park
text:
PRINCE GEORGE’S COUNTY, Md. (WJLA) — An investigation is underway after human remains were found inside a burning vehicle at Whitfield Chapel Park in Prince George’s County on Thursday night.
Maryland-National Capital Park Police said someone passing the park a little before 10:30 p.m. saw flames. The Prince George’s County Fire Department said it put out the fire. Firefighters then found human remains inside the burned vehicle, according to the department.
Investigation
Prince George’s County police were leading the investigation. Homicide detectives were working with fire investigators on the case.
It remained unclear whether the death was a homicide or a suicide. Police have not released the name or gender of the victim.
Residents react
Maya Wilson, an Upper Marlboro resident, said she was walking in the park Friday with another woman.
“That is crazy that that happened one hundred feet away from us right now,” Wilson said.
Wilson and the other woman said it is nerve-wracking not knowing what led to the incident.
Janiya Prescott, a nearby resident, said she has been coming to the park since she was a child.
“I’ve been here since I was a kid, so it’s like, do I want to come here again?” Prescott said.
Nearby residents described the community and the park as normally quiet.
“A lot of people come here; they play kickball, they play baseball,” Prescott said.
“It’s always been pleasant out here. No problems at all,” said Jerry Blue, a nearby resident.

title: Judge accepts ex-NFL star Antonio Brown’s guilty plea to reduced charge, sentences probation
text:
MIAMI (AP) — Former NFL star Antonio Brown pleaded guilty Friday to aggravated assault with a firearm in connection with a 2025 shooting outside a celebrity boxing match in Miami.
Judge Marisa Tinkler Mendez sentenced Brown to three years of probation, during which time he will have to attend weekly counseling sessions and not possess a firearm, among other conditions.
Wearing a black leather jacket and white pants, he spoke sparingly and in a low voice during the brief proceedings in Miami state court. As he entered his guilty plea, the judge asked him to speak up.
Outside the courtroom, Brown thanked God and said he wanted to “get back to life” and his family.
He declined to answer other questions, but his lawyer, Mark Eiglarsh, said they were “extremely grateful” the case was behind them.
“My client was facing 30 years in prison with a 20-year minimum mandatory, and he was given an offer he just couldn’t refuse,” he said. “Probation was too good to turn down, and we’re both very excited about the outcome.”
The plea to the reduced charge allows the All-Pro wide receiver to avoid prison time and a criminal conviction.
Brown had initially been charged with attempted murder after police say he grabbed a handgun from a security staffer at the event and fired two shots at a man he had been in a fistfight with earlier.
Brown, 38, maintained he was defending himself from an attack as others were trying to steal jewelry from him.
Florida’s Stand Your Ground law allows people who believe they face death or serious injury to use deadly force to defend themselves without a duty to retreat.
Prosecutor Howard Rosen said in court Friday that his office was seeking to reduce the charge against Brown because there was “a question” of whether he was actually attempting to shoot the victim, who had been walking away from the altercation at the time.
He noted the victim, who was grazed in the neck, was in court for the hearing and has said publicly that he wouldn’t cooperate with police and didn’t want to press charges.
“Rather than the entire case going away and there being no opportunity for Mr. Brown to receive what’s ultimately going to be some therapeutic treatment, we all came together — the defense and the state — and decided that this was in the best interest of everybody,” Rosen said.
The victim, Zul-Qarnain Kwame Nantambu, has said previously that he’s since forgiven Brown.
“We are grateful to the Court for ratifying this carefully crafted agreement,” Richard Cooper, his lawyer, said in a statement. “We have maintained that we wish Mr. Brown healing and a path closer to God.”
Brown spent 12 years in the NFL, most of it with the Pittsburgh Steelers. He won a Super Bowl with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2021 under quarterback Tom Brady.
The following season, though, Brown effectively ended his career when he inexplicably took off his jersey, shoulder pads and gloves and ran off the field during a game. The Buccaneers released him after the incident.
Brown has dealt with other legal problems in recent years.
He previously was accused of battery on a moving truck driver, several domestic violence charges, failure to pay child support and other incidents.
Brown was extradited in November 2025 from Dubai, where he has business interests, after an arrest warrant on the attempted murder charge was issued in June of the same year.
___
Marcelo reported from New York.

Prosecutor Howard Rosen said in court Friday that his office was seeking to reduce the charge against Brown because there was “a question” of whether he was actually attempting to shoot the victim, who had been walking away from the altercation at the time.
He noted the victim, who was grazed in the neck, was in court for the hearing and has said publicly that he wouldn’t cooperate with police and didn’t want to press charges.
“Rather than the entire case going away and there being no opportunity for Mr. Brown to receive what’s ultimately going to be some therapeutic treatment, we all came together — the defense and the state — and decided that this was in the best interest of everybody,” Rosen said.
The victim, Zul-Qarnain Kwame Nantambu, has said previously that he’s since forgiven Brown.
“We are grateful to the Court for ratifying this carefully crafted agreement,” Richard Cooper, his lawyer, said in a statement. “We have maintained that we wish Mr. Brown healing and a path closer to God.”
Brown spent 12 years in the NFL, most of it with the Pittsburgh Steelers. He won a Super Bowl with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2021 under quarterback Tom Brady.
The following season, though, Brown effectively ended his career when he inexplicably took off his jersey, shoulder pads and gloves and ran off the field during a game. The Buccaneers released him after the incident.
Brown has dealt with other legal problems in recent years.
He previously was accused of battery on a moving truck driver, several domestic violence charges, failure to pay child support and other incidents.
Brown was extradited in November 2025 from Dubai, where he has business interests, after an arrest warrant on the attempted murder charge was issued in June of the same year.
___
Marcelo reported from New York.

title: Youth field hockey is growing. High school coaches hope it will save the sport.
text:
We’re proud to make high school sports coverage free for everyone, because these moments matter. At Maine State Credit Union, we’re here for the people and places that make Maine strong. Let’s go! Learn more at mainestatecu.org. 
Impressive as 17 wins this season are, that’s not the most startling number the Mt. Ararat High field hockey team and coach Krista Chase have seen this season.
That would be the 80 players who turned out this fall for Mt. Ararat’s Baby Eagles youth program, the pre-kindergarten through eighth grade feeder system for the Topsham school’s varsity and junior varsity teams.
It’s made the Eagles, who fell just short against Cheverus for the Class A title on Saturday, the envy of a sport struggling to keep players. Thirty-five players began the fall in the middle school program. Forty-one turned out for the high school team.
It’s hard to find better numbers at any other school in Maine. And, as Chase said, it comes from the ground up.
“That is a direct result of youth programs,” Chase said. “Because these girls have grown up in youth programs. There is a direct correlation. All of us coaches who are working crazy extra hours to provide good youth programs, we’re doing it for a reason.”
Mt. Ararat is not the only school seeing results. Youth field hockey is gaining steam. New programs are popping up. Players are getting started earlier. Competition is becoming more robust. Opportunities to play are more plentiful.
“When I took over 13 years ago … I needed to get sticks in girls’ hands earlier,” Chase said. “I’m not alone in that anymore … and it’s paying off.”
Just ask Kate Brunelle, who started a Portland youth program three years ago and is seeing booming numbers. Or Winslow coach Mary Beth Bourgoin, whose youth round robin last October had more teams participating than at any other point. Or Yarmouth coach Bre Page, who has seen the numbers in her youth program climb by more than 30 participants in three years.
“Now we have 3-year-olds out there with sticks flying around. It’s crazy,” Page said. “It’s hard to get those youth kids, but we’re getting them. … The sport’s growing, and I think it shows at every level.”
COMBATING A TREND
All coaches point to the same motivation: “We’re trying to save our programs,” Bourgoin said.
Any good news comes not a moment too soon, as the high school game has continued to endure the body blows of low turnout. According to the National Federation of State High School Associations, the number of girls in Maine playing field hockey shrank from 2,618 in 2009 to 1,809 in 2024, and then to 1,578 last year.
Just this year, Kennebunk had to merge with Sanford to continue playing, John Bapst combined with Bangor, and Oceanside announced it will play a JV schedule next year. The Maine Field Hockey Association has for the past couple of years had discussions with the Maine Principals’ Association about adding 7-on-7 or 8-on-8 field hockey.
It’s led communities to realize that bolstering the youth programs is a now-or-never move to get the sport to flourish — or simply survive.
“There are a lot of schools … who have always had strong youth programs,” Chase said. “And there are others who have seen the writing on the wall with the trends in field hockey numbers in Maine, and they’re working their tails off to combat that.”
For years, field hockey lagged behind in the youth sports scene, particularly in southern Maine where soccer is king. Field hockey was often not introduced until middle school, putting it behind in drawing and keeping players, and in many of the communities where it was offered, it was less organized and less structured.
“Soccer has pretty much been the same since, I don’t know, probably 20-something years,” Biddeford field hockey coach Caitlin Tremberth said. “Field hockey wasn’t taken as seriously.”
That’s changing. Bourgoin said she’s seen a shift in the philosophy of youth programs, from recreational practices to the formation of teams that travel to different towns for play days every week. The thinking, she said, is that the more competitive the sport is, the more kids are going to want to stick with it.
Bourgoin started her rec program at Winslow in 2002. Twenty years later, she set up a travel team and had 22 kids join up. The team has players in second through fifth grades.
“Parents today want their kid part of a team. That’s why I did it,” she said. “It had to do with offering something more competitive than just coming on Sundays, doing skills and then playing for a little bit. … (I said) ‘If we want our program to survive and get the numbers going, this has to happen.'”
In the Portland area, Kate Brunelle began Portland Youth Field Hockey in 2024. There was no feeder program in Maine’s largest city before that.
“If you were a Portland parent … you’d have to go to other towns,” said Brunelle, whose daughters Sydney (a senior) and Brooke (a sophomore) star for Cheverus. “Kids (in high school) were getting cut from their soccer teams, and field hockey was begging for kids. So it just seemed like this was something we had to do.”
Portland Youth Field Hockey started with 11 players. This year, the number has climbed to 66 with a wait list, and there are teams for kindergarten through sixth grade. Spurred by that growth, Brunelle started Maine Youth Field Hockey this year, connecting Portland with other southern Maine programs.
“We were tapping this untapped market of kids,” she said. “It wasn’t as if field hockey disappeared. It was just that field hockey hadn’t evolved the way that I think some of these other sports had. This effort is really to reverse that trend a little bit.”
TIME AND RESOURCES
Other pockets of the state have seen a boost. Page’s program at Yarmouth, which had fewer than 20 players when she took over in 2023, was up to 52 this year. Burgess LePage, who coaches Greely of Cumberland, had 85 players at her September play day, compared with 61 last year. Dirigo of Dixfield and Mountain Valley of Rumford, which formerly combined for a team, had enough players to field their own teams this year.
Betsy Dorr, who coordinates youth field hockey in central Maine and is the commissioner of Area Youth Sports in Jay and Livermore Falls, said “there’s definitely more opportunities” for young girls to play.
“Our Pre-K to first grade never competed in any play days. And now I’m like, there’s no reason we can’t get these girls to get out and get that experience with playing,” said Dorr, whose numbers rose by 20 this year. “Getting those girls out there makes them want to come back.”
So, how have they done it? For Page, getting her varsity players to help teach kids was key, as was holding clinics in the spring to give kids a chance to give the sport a try.
“(They were) super cheap, just to try to get people here,” Page said. “You don’t need equipment, just try it out. One hour, come try it out, and we got so many kids.”
In some cases, the availability of a turf field has driven interest by allowing for more field access, higher-capacity play days and an easier game to learn. In others, the key ingredient has been having a varsity coach with the time and energy to spend seven days a week coaching all levels.
“It’s most likely going to be your personal time,” said Caitlin Tremberth, Biddeford’s coach since 2014. “You’re not going to get paid extra.”
Brunelle said her efforts to get youth field hockey going in Portland accelerated when the city’s recreation department partnered with the program, providing equipment, money and field access, as well as a way to spread the word.
“(They) helped us get access to the people of Portland,” she said. “That’s a really big part of what we need. We need resources.”
When those factors aren’t in place, growth is difficult. Camden Hills coach Lindsey Clement operates summer and indoor winter programs for kindergarten through eighth grade that have remained steady with around 40 and 35 players, respectively.
Getting more players, though, is tough. There aren’t many schools and field hockey-rich cultures nearby for the Rockport-based program to draw from; the high school’s grass field isn’t available in the summer, which forces trips to Northport to play; and Clement and her staff, who used to take youth teams to play in a league at Hampden Academy on Sundays, don’t have the time to travel with those games now on Saturdays.
“To have 50 kids in a youth program, that would be amazing, but I don’t ever see that being feasible for Camden Hills,” she said. “It’s an uphill battle.”
Clement does, though, see signs of growth around the state. And coaches who have been worried about the sport’s long-term health are feeling encouraged.
“Oh, my God, it’s totally going to save it,” Tremberth said. “There never was a prominent youth presence 15 years ago. Now you can see the numbers staying steady, and some are going up.”
Bourgoin at Winslow spoke with cautious optimism.
“The word is ‘hopeful,'” she said. “I feel it’s bigger and it’s growing. You have other towns that are also really trying to start up. … I think it’s getting bigger, which should help in the long run with numbers.”

title: Trump offers UFC chief Dana White press secretary job
text:
(Gray News) - President Donald Trump offered UFC president and CEO Dana White the job of press secretary on Saturday.
In a post on Truth Social, Trump said: “I am pleased to announce that the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior, has been offered the job of Press Secretary of the United States.”
The president also said the offer extended to White’s assistants, “even though some are not from our Country.”
“We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left,” Trump wrote. “Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other. Dana, please take the job!”
In response to Trump, White posted a photo on Instagram Stories of himself standing behind the press secretary’s lectern in the White House, captioned, “On to the next chapter.”
It was unclear whether White has accepted the position or is simply acknowledging the president’s request in jest.
In October, White House press secretary Katie Zacharia left the position just five days after her stint as Karoline Leavitt’s replacement began.
The president told reporters he suggested Zacharia quit after her first and only press briefing.
The president’s appeal to White follows Friday’s announcement that Trump’s deputy chief of staff, Stephen Miller, would be promoted to chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles.

title: Maranacook girls soccer shuts out Fort Kent for 2nd straight Class C title
text:
Our Communities. Our Teams. Our Future.
We’re proud to make high school sports coverage free for everyone—because these moments matter. At Maine State Credit Union, we’re here for the people and places that make Maine strong. Let’s Go! Learn more at mainestatecu.org. 
LEWISTON — In the moment, Evelyn Stevenson couldn’t believe her good fortune.
With 9:06 remaining in the Class C girls soccer final on Saturday, a through pass found Stevenson’s foot, about 15 yards from the net with no defenders around her.
Stevenson drilled her shot into the top of the goal, sealing a 2-0 victory for Maranacook over Fort Kent at Lewiston High’s Don Roux Field.
“I’m honestly surprised it went in,” Stevenson laughed.
Stevenson, a senior forward, scored both goals for the Black Bears. It’s the second straight Gold Ball for Maranacook, both wins coming against the Warriors. It’s also the third state title in program history, all in the last six seasons. The Black Bears beat Bucksport 5-0 in 2021.
“It never gets old,” said Maranacook coach Travis Magnusson. “This is the toughest one we’ve ever had. It was a great state game. Every team we played in the playoffs — Waynflete, Hall-Dale, Mt. Abram — they all could have gone either way. It’s been a crazy season.”
The Black Bears lost only once, going 17-1 for the season. Fort Kent, the North champion, finished 14-2-2.
While Stevenson had two goals, the game was a showcase of Maranacook’s defense, which did not allow a goal throughout the Class C tournament. The defensive group, which included senior Cooper Davis, junior Lydia Stevenson and senior Eve Simcock, kept scoring opportunities for the Warriors at a minimum. When they did arise, keeper Stella Stewart turned the opportunities away. Stewart, a senior, recorded four saves.
“There were certainly moments where we were stressed, but we played as a team on this defense,” Davis said. “We communicate, we back each other up. If one makes a mistake, the next one is there.”
Maranacook dominated possession in the first half and struck early, taking a 1-0 lead just 2:03 in. Haley Berube sent a cross to her right, finding Stevenson open in front of the net. Stevenson knocked her shot toward the top of the net, above the leaping arms of Fort Kent keeper Trinity Daigle.
“We pretended that it was still 0-0 (after the goal),” Stewart said. “Everything can change in a split second, and we knew we still had to work our butts off. We still had (78) minutes left in the game. A lot can happen in that time.”
The Warriors turned up their offensive pressure in the second half but managed only three shots on goal. The Black Bears had only one shot but made it count, with Stevenson’s game-sealing score.
Maranacook outscored opponents by an 8-0 margin in its four tournament games. All three of the Black Bears’ state championship game wins have been shutouts.
“We played our best in the playoffs, for sure,” Magnusson said. “It helps when you have a goalie as confident as (Stewart), and (Davis) is as good as we’ve ever had, anywhere, with (Simcock), defensively. And then (Stevenson, offensively). Those seniors led us.”

title: 82-year-old man dies after getting hit by his own car
text:
SAINT STEPHEN, S.C. (WCSC/Gray News) — An 82-year-old man in South Carolina was hit and killed by his own car in an apparent mishap, according to authorities.
The Berkeley County Coroner’s Office reported that Gilbert King, of St. Stephen, died Thursday afternoon.
Coroner Darnell Hartwell said King accidentally put his car in reverse instead of putting it in park before getting out of the car.
As he got out, King was hit by the vehicle and suffered fatal injuries.
The coroner and the South Carolina Highway Patrol are investigating.

title: What to know about the hoax bomb threats that targeted flights in Europe
text:
What to know about the hoax bomb threats that targeted flights in Europe
Bomb threats targeted dozens of flights across Europe this week following a string of hoaxes that caused flight diversions and forced airlines to scramble to keep passengers safe and air traffic disruptions minimal.
Related video above: Google analyzed 5 years of flight data. Thanksgiving and Christmas fares may be cheapest sooner than you think
Fake bomb threats are relatively common, but it is unusual to see so many in such a short period. No suspicious items were found and no one has been injured, but the threats raised concerns because they came on the heels of other European disruptions — including attacks on supermarket refrigeration systems and drone incursions.
With unanswered questions hanging over the continent — it was not known whether the threats were linked, who sent them or what they hoped to achieve — security experts were to meet in Brussels next week to discuss measures to deal with the hoaxes.
Here's what to know:
Dozens of flights across Europe have been targeted
The hoaxes have led to plane searches and diversions, and, in some cases, emergency landings and military escorts.
Still, the European air traffic authority insisted that overall, the threats caused minimal disruption to aviation.
Separately, three broadcasters — the Irish national broadcaster RTE, the U.K.-based Sky and NOVA TV, a private broadcaster in Bulgaria — also received security threats on Friday, a possible sign the menace was spreading beyond the skies.
And on Saturday, Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said his personal data had been disseminated on the dark web, an encrypted part of the internet, and that he has been exposed to "threats and intimidation."
Italian Premier Giorgia Meloni blamed pro-Russian hackers for the leak.
Tajani, who is also a vice premier in Italy's government, did not specify what kind of information had been shared, but suggested that the cyberthreat was ongoing. He did not indicate who might be responsible for the cyberattack but reiterated the Italian government's support for Ukraine.
No word on who is behind the threats
It remains unclear who is behind the airline threats, which come at a time of increased geopolitical tensions and warnings from authorities that Russia may be ramping up its so-called hybrid threats in Europe — a mix of covert and indirect attacks attributed to Moscow and meant to destabilize European countries.
Authorities haven't attributed the threats to any group or state actor, and no evidence has emerged linking the hoaxes to a government. An email containing the threat sent Thursday to airport authorities in Rome and reviewed by The Associated Press purported to come from a group describing itself as anti-feminist and claiming it was targeting a "feminist regime."
Another European airport received a threat with similar wording, but it was unclear if it came from the same sender.
In Amsterdam, meanwhile, the Dutch Marechaussee military police detained a man on Thursday night at Amsterdam's Schiphol Airport in connection with a threat to a flight that was about to leave for Prague, Marechaussee spokesperson Doron Wallin said Saturday.
It was not clear if the threat was linked to other recent hoaxes. Wallin said the Marechaussee regularly deals with fake bomb threats. The aircraft flew on to Prague later in the evening, and the man was released the following day.
Expert says travelers should not be alarmed
Matthew Borie of Osprey Flight Solutions, which advises airlines on flight threats, said he had several hypotheses for the incidents — ranging from a single threat triggering copycat incidents to an individual or a group making multiple threats, and "hybrid warfare" operations by state actors or their supporters.
The focus on Europe means "there could be a Russian angle," said Borie, the company's co-founder and chief intelligence officer. "We need to keep in mind, though, that Iranian hybrid warfare is just as active in certain pockets of Europe as well."
His message for travelers?
"Don't be alarmed," he said, noting that national authorities have "coordinated response mechanisms," including, at times, the deployment of NATO fighter jets to escort such planes.
Jacob Funk Kirkegaard, a senior fellow at the Bruegel think tank in Brussels, said the threats were "stress-testing" how European governments and airport officials respond, and whether their responses were coordinated.
The idea behind the threats "appears to be to sow chaos, uncertainty, about the reliability of air traffic across Europe" and could have "cascading effects" — such as economic damage and costs related to inspection, investigation and the cleaning of aircraft.

title: Wisdom girls soccer defeats Bangor Christian in 8-person final
text:
We’re proud to make high school sports coverage free for everyone—because these moments matter. At Maine State Credit Union, we’re here for the people and places that make Maine strong. Let’s Go! Learn more at mainestatecu.org. 
Wisdom earned redemption against Bangor Christian to capture its first girls soccer state title.
The Pioneers scored three second-half goals, including two by Ellie Cyr, and defeated the Patriots 3-1 in the 8-person girls final on Saturday in a rematch of last year’s state championship, which Bangor Christian won 3-0.
The Patriots also recorded 2-0 and 3-2 regular-season victories over Wisdom. It looked like South regional champion Bangor Christian (17-1) was on its way to another big triumph when Rivers Bradford’s goal gave the Patriots a 1-0 lead with 16:45 remaining in the first half.
Emma Soucy put the Pioneers (16-2) on the board when her free kick from near midfield bounced into the 18-yard box, got past Bangor Christian goalkeeper Addison Tucker and rolled into the goal with 18:25 remaining in the game.
Wisdom took the lead with under 11 minutes to play when Ellie Cyr’s free kick from just outside the box found the mark.
After Tucker tried to move the ball upfield for the Patriots, Cyr booted it back over Tucker and into an unguarded net to make it 3-1 with 1:13 remaining.
Tucker finished with two saves. Mikayl Michaud made eight stops for Wisdom.

title: Maine Lobstermen's Association welcomes change in federal whale policy
main_topic: Jobs, housing, and cost of living
text:
The Maine Lobstermen’ s Association said the federal government has made a major shift in its federal whale policy that had threatened the crucial state industry.
“The Maine Lobstermen’s Association welcomes a major shift in federal whale policy following its landmark court victory against the National Marine Fisheries Service,” the trade industry group stated in a Nov. 6 news release.
On Nov. 5, NMFS announced that new scientific analyses indicate U.S. fisheries may be meeting the federal standard for protecting endangered North Atlantic right whales.
“(This was) a dramatic change from the government’s previous assessments that misapplied the science and the law, threatened the future of Maine’s lobster industry, and were ultimately ruled unlawful,” the news release stated.
“The announcement marks a significant turning point after years of uncertainty for Maine’s lobster industry caused by the threat of increasingly severe federal regulations that were not justified by available scientific observations or the law. It follows MLA’s successful federal court challenge, which overturned NMFS’s misinterpretation of the law and unjustified reliance on worst-case assumptions in assessing the lobster fishery’s impact on right whales,” the release stated.
“This is what we fought for. MLA took the federal government to court and won because its claims about our fishery weren’t supported by the science or the law,” said Patrice McCarron, MLA Executive Director. “That court victory forced NMFS to change course. Now the government’s own analysis is beginning to confirm what Maine lobstermen have been saying for years.”
In June 2023, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit agreed with the Association, the Maine Department of Marine Resources, the Maine Lobstering Union, and the Massachusetts Lobstermen’s Association that NMFS distorted the science driving the regulation, relying improperly on assumptions and worst-case scenarios when determining the risk posed by industry to right whales.
That Appeals Court ruling had overturned an earlier District Court ruling in favor of the federal government. The Association had filed its legal challenge in 2022.
The court’s decision allowed the current regulation to remain in effect while NMFS developed a new rule. Congress had earlier voted to delay further rulemaking until 2028.
Maine lobster harvesters landed 78.8 million pounds in 2025, down from the more than 100 million pounds regularly caught during the 2010s boom. But the value of the fishery remained high at $461.4 million on the strength of a $5.85 per pound boat price, the third highest price on record, driven by strong consumer demand.
In Knox County, which follows only Hancock County in Maine lobster landings, harvesters landed 20.6 million pounds last year, with a value of $124.4 million. Several Knox towns were again among Maine’s biggest lobster ports, with Stonington leading the state, followed by Vinalhaven, Portland, Friendship and Spruce Head.
