title: Melania Trump, LSU are set to announce a scholarship program for students who were in foster care
text:
Melania Trump and LSU announce $7.2M to endow scholarships for former foster care students
Melania Trump on Saturday announced that Louisiana State University has raised $7.2 million to provide scholarships through her “Fostering the Future” program to LSU students who were formerly in foster care.
"This achievement will give young people from foster care an anchor of stability, a strong educational foundation and a chance to build a wonderful life,” she said at an event with LSU President Wade Rousse and some of the donors.
The $7.2 million in private donations will fund a permanent endowment for the scholarships, speakers said. MMR Group Inc., an electrical contracting company based in Baton Rouge, committed $5 million, with members of the LSU Foundation raising an additional $2.2 million, they said.
Related video above: Related video above: First Lady Melania Trump hosts Fostering the Future event
The first lady later attended the football game between college regional rivals, LSU and Alabama, another participant in the initiative.
“As adults, we have a moral obligation to our children, especially those in foster care. But, as you know, we must act to truly make a difference. The foster care community doesn’t need words,” she added. She concluded her brief remarks with, "Now, let’s go and enjoy the game.”
LSU has 14 scholars under the program and Alabama has nine, she said, part of a group of 100 students supported across 26 participating colleges and universities this semester.
The foster care program was featured across campus and at Tiger Stadium. The first lady watched the game from an enclosed box, and LSU players sported the logo of her “Be Best” initiative on their helmets and uniforms. Fans received commemorative white “Be Best” towels to wave during the game.
“Fostering the Future” is an offshoot of the “Be Best” child well-being initiative that was her signature platform during President Donald Trump’s first term.
Television cameras also panned to Melania Trump in the box during the performance of the national anthem and later when a group of “Fostering the Future” scholars were recognized on the field. Cheers rose from the stadium when she appeared on the stadium's screens. At one point, Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry was seen chatting with her in the suite.
Her commemorative coin was flipped during the coin toss, the White House said.
During the scholarship announcement, Rousse presented Melania Trump with an LSU helmet sporting the “Be Best” logo and an LSU jersey with her first name and the number 14, representing the number of enrolled scholars.
“At LSU, we believe talent is everywhere, but we understand that opportunity is not,” Rousse said. "That is why access is one of our highest priorities. Students who have experienced foster care have already demonstrated resilience, determination and potential. Our responsibility, our responsibility is to make sure circumstances beyond their control do not stand between them and a life-changing higher educational experience.”
The first lady started to work on foster care issues after the Republican president left office in 2021 and created “Fostering the Future” to provide resources and support, including scholarships.
Earlier this year, Melania Trump was on Capitol Hill to push Congress to pass a legislative package that would broaden access to services for young people in foster care by updating a decades-old program. The measures cleared the House and are pending in the Senate.
She told members of the House Ways and Means Committee that young people in foster care face barriers to housing, transportation and other challenges outside of the classroom that affect their performance in school along with their future financial independence.
Last November, the first lady spearheaded an executive order signed by the president linking the federal government, colleges and universities, the private sector and charitable groups to create educational and employment opportunities for those in foster care.
She also created “Fostering the Future Together,” a global version of the program with more than 45 participating countries.

title: Four-vehicle crash snarls northbound traffic along I-95 in Bangor
text:
Police responded to a four-vehicle crash along I-95 in Bangor late Saturday morning.
The crash occurred on the KD Stream Bridge in the northbound lane, said Maj. Aaron Turcotte, a spokesperson for the Maine State Police, which patrols the interstate. Responding officers had to move cars off the highway onto Broadway in Bangor, he said around noon.
There did not appear to be any injuries from the crash, the major said.

title: Alaska Senate race remains undecided days after Election Day
text:
WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - Fewer than 700 votes separated the top two candidates in Alaska’s Senate race Friday with 74% of ballots counted. Democrat Mary Peltola led Republican incumbent Sen. Dan Sullivan by a slim margin, which had not changed in more than 24 hours.
As polls closed on Election Day and states began to turn blue or red, Mississippi and Alaska were the only two states left without a new senator.
As Americans keep an eye out for updates on the Last Frontier, Peltola reminded supporters that a long count is not new for Alaska.
“The results are not gonna be fast, but Alaskans are patient... It will be weeks. We know this. We know this. This is how it’s always been. This is normal. This is Alaska normal,” Peltola said.
Alaska has a ranked choice voting system, with ballots tallied in rounds. In a general election, a candidate must reach 50% or more of the vote to win.
If no candidate reaches 50% using first-place votes, officials take the last-place finisher and reallocate those ballots to voters’ second and third choices. That tabulation will not happen before Nov. 18.
Ballots also must be flown in or mailed from hard-to-reach areas of Alaska, meaning the process usually is lengthy, though this year is different.
Sullivan was not the only Dan on the ballot. Another Dan Sullivan was listed as a third-party option. The Justice Department and the FBI are now investigating.
“What’s the first order of business when [Peltola is] going to run for the Senate, to put together a secret scheme. To trick Alaskans to throw away their vote and rig the election,” Sullivan said.
The Trump administration sued to stop the election from being certified if Peltola wins. The administration claimed Democrats plotted to add the same-named candidate as a ploy to pull votes.

title: Footage shows bodies at the home of the man behind mass shooting in Polish city, prime minister says
text:
KRAKOW, Poland (AP) — A Polish man with far-right views drove into a busy central square in Krakow on Saturday and opened fire, killing six people and injuring 15 others before police shot and wounded him, authorities said.
“Everything indicates that he was fascinated by far-right ideologies,” Kierwiński said at a news conference.
Hours after the attack, Prime Minister Donald Tusk said authorities found the bodies of three of the suspect’s close family members — two women and a man — inside of his home in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski, a city about 150 kilometers (93 miles) northeast of Krakow.
“We have the next acts of this tragedy,” Tusk told reporters.
Four women and two men were killed in the Krakow attack. At least three of the women were Polish, and one of the dead was a U.K. citizen, authorities said. Police were still trying to identify the other two people who were killed.
A total of 13 people were hospitalized in serious condition, authorities said, though that figure may include the gunman, who underwent surgery after the attack.
It’s unclear how many of the injured were shot. Two of them were treated and released within hours of the mass shooting. Two police officers were seriously injured, Kierwiński said. Five non-Poles were also injured, police commander Marek Boroń said.
People were wounded at several locations
The attacker wore military-style fatigues and a bulletproof vest, and used a military-type long gun, Krakow police spokesperson Katarzyna Cisło said. Police found other weapons and ammunition in his car. He kept firing at the police even after being shot himself, she said.
The attacker engaged in a “wild ride” around Main Square, which is why people were wounded at several locations, said Cisło, adding that the gunman appears to have acted alone.
“The square will belong to us again,” Gibała said in a video posted on X.
Mass shootings are rare in Poland
Photos showed a Polish Medical Air Rescue helicopter after it landed in the square.
It wasn’t immediately clear whether the gun used in the attack or those found in the attacker’s car are legal. Around 411,000 people hold gun permits in Poland, which has a population of 37 million, and interest in gun ownership has been rising.
The Krakow attacker’s military gear, guns and overall look were similar to those of other “extreme right lone actors” committing attacks around Europe, said Kacper Rekawek, a senior researcher at the International Center for Counterterrorism in The Hague. “We have had attempts before, but now we can say that these kinds of attacks have become successful in Poland.”

Ciobanu reported from Warsaw, Poland, and Dazio reported from Berlin.

title: Mother sentenced to life in prison for murdering 4-year-old, abandoning 1-year-old on interstate
text:
LAKE CHARLES, La. (KPLC/Gray News) - A mother in Louisiana was sentenced to life in prison for killing her 4-year-old child and abandoning her baby near an interstate.
Aaliyah Jack, 28, was sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole for killing her son, Legend, and 15 years for cruelty to juveniles for abandoning her 1-year-old child, Kingtrail.
Legend had been living with his paternal grandmother, Dion Polk, since May 2024. Polk said she dropped him off with Jack’s mother on July 6, 2024, after which Jack ran off with him and Kingtrail.
Legend’s body was found in the water near an interstate welcome center two days later. A truck driver spotted Kingtrail crawling along I-10 just a few miles away the next morning.
Jack was arrested in Mississippi the same day Kingtrail was rescued. She was later charged with second-degree murder and cruelty to a juvenile.
When deputies brought Jack to the Calcasieu Correctional Center on July 20, she told a KPLC reporter that she had killed Legend and abandoned Kingtrail while “under the influence of drugs.”
A Calcasieu Parish jury convicted Jack of second-degree murder and child cruelty in September after seeing Legend’s autopsy photos and hearing from detectives and family members.
While the murder conviction came with a mandatory life sentence, a decision had to be made regarding the cruelty to juveniles charge.
Jack made a statement in court that was hard to follow and repeatedly said she did not know what to say.
During the sentencing, Jack did not apologize and instead talked about spending money for someone’s birthday. It was unclear who she was referring to.
Ultimately, the judge ruled that Jack had shown deliberate cruelty to both victims.
The prosecution says justice was served.
“I am always sorry for the families on both sides. Nobody wins here. I believe that justice was done. I believe that Ms. Jack is going to spend the rest of her life in prison, which is where she belongs, because of the nature of what she did,” first assistant district attorney Jacob Johnson said.

title: Maine should be rallying behind clean energy permitting reform
also_topics: Jobs, housing, and cost of living
text:
I was disappointed to see Attorney General Aaron Frey sign a letter to Senate leadership (Oct. 21) opposing the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA).
Mainers pay some of the highest electricity rates in the country, driven largely by our dependence on out-of-state fossil fuels, particularly natural gas. Lowering electricity costs and meeting our climate goals can go hand in hand. Maine has abundant, low-cost clean energy waiting to come online; transmission and other infrastructure upgrades are needed to deliver it.
New England Clean Energy Connect (NECEC) is now delivering clean Canadian hydropower to New England, displacing fossil fuel generation. Its completion should be a point of pride. Instead, years of lawsuits and political battles added more than $500 million to its cost — a burden that ultimately falls on ratepayers.
BAAJA would help prevent such delays without weakening environmental protections. It establishes reasonable timelines for project reviews and legal challenges while preserving the authority of courts. It also limits arbitrary permit revocations that have stalled offshore wind and other renewable energy projects.
The bill further ensures that data centers pay for the grid upgrades they require, rather than passing those costs to Maine families.
Maine has a proud tradition of putting results ahead of party politics. I hope Sen. Collins makes BAAJA a priority before the end of her term and Sen. King supports it when the Senate considers the bill this month. I hope Attorney General Frey takes another look as well.
Mainers cannot afford another NECEC.
Don Parent
Cumberland
